rationale_overall: Filtered out substantial noise: youth/school robotics competitions (Octobots, Wildwood, Wolfpack, FIRST Robotics regionals), generic AI think-pieces and clickbait 'best AI stock' listicles (Fool.com x5, SoundHound, Apple), foreign/non-investable items (Samsung profit, China DeepSeek-Huawei, China satellite launches, South Korea's Kori-2 restart, Taiwan quantum push, China nuclear-for-AI), Iran/Israel/Gulf missile-strike geopolitical events with no directly investable US ticker attached, and vague government/supply-chain press releases (Saskatchewan uranium mines, SMR supply-chain grant, INL microreactor test bed) that name no tradeable vehicle. Remaining signal was supportive-but-incremental for existing holdings only: NVDA's $2B Marvell data-center-fabric deal and TSMC's record AI-chip revenue reinforce the AI holding (NVDA/GOOGL) without surfacing a stronger, cheaper emerging name; RKLB's 2% pop is routine price action, not a new catalyst; SMR's thesis (Kori restart, uranium mine approvals, microreactor test bed) remains intact but these are foreign/government items, not new-ticker catalysts. Northrop Grumman's Hungary satellite contract and Mercury Systems' missile-tracking-satellite recorder deal are minor single-contract defense/geopolitical items -- interesting for the rearmament wave longer-term but too thin to justify displacing a current core holding this week. No candidate cleared the bar of a genuine rising-wave catalyst stronger than an existing holding, so the watchlist is left unchanged this cycle.
